 Judgment
This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the death of Sri. Chowdaiah S.R. S/o Ramachandran S., in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioners that on 06.05.2023 at about 2:45 P.M., the deceased,
Chowdaiah, was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing registration No.
KA-06-EZ-1327.

The rider was riding the said motorcycle on the Bengaluru-Gowribidanur Road,
near D-cross Circle, Doddaballapura Town, Bengaluru District.

At that time, the driver of the Mahindra XUV-300 car bearing registration No. KA-17-MA-1497 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle") drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the motorcycle.
3. Due to the tremendous impact of the accident, both the rider and the pillion rider sustained severe injuries all over their bodies.
Immediately after the accident, Chowdaiah was shifted to Aster CMI Hospital, Bengaluru, where despite expert medical treatment, he succumbed to the fatal injuries on 08.05.2023 at about 11:20 P.M.

Thereafter, a post- mortem examination was conducted at the Government Hospital, Doddaballapura, and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners, who performed the last rites and funeral ceremonies.
4. At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged about 72 years.
He was a retired Gynecologist from Government service.
After retirement, he was engaged in part-time medical practice and was earning approximately Rs.1,10,000/- per month.
The deceased was contributing his income towards the maintenance and welfare of his family.
5. Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners have suffered mental shock, agony, and financial loss.

Hence,
the petitioners have prayed that this Tribunal be pleased to award compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-

2 with interest from Respondent Nos.1 and 3, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, in the interest of justice and equity.

sentences.text: 6. In response to the petition, Respondent Nos.1 and 3 have appeared before this Tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their written statements.
Initially, Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company was wrongly arrayed as a party to the proceedings and subsequently, the said respondent was deleted from the array of parties.

7. Respondent No.1, being the RC owner of the offending vehicle, has filed his written statement admitting that he is the registered owner of the offending car and that the said vehicle was insured with Respondent No.3 under a valid and effective insurance policy as on the date of the accident.
However, he has denied the age, avocation, and income of the deceased, as well as the relationship and dependency of the petitioners on the deceased.
He has further contended that he was not driving the car at the time of the accident and that the driver has not been made a party to the proceedings.

He has specifically contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle rider, in which the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider, allegedly without wearing a helmet and without observing traffic rules, particularly when the signal was red.
Hence, he has asserted that the accident did not occur due to the negligence of the driver of the offending car and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
8. Respondent No.3 - the insurer - has filed its written statement admitting the issuance of the insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
However, it has contended that its liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The insurer has denied the occurrence of the accident as alleged and also denied the involvement of the offending vehicle.
Further, it has contended that the driver of the offending car did not possess a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident, thereby alleging breach of policy conditions.

9. Respondent No.3 has also denied that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending car and has instead contended that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the motorcycle rider, in which the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider.
It has further raised a contention of non-joinder of necessary parties on the ground that the owner and insurer of the motorcycle have not been arrayed as respondents in the petition.
Additionally, Respondent No.3 has contended that there is non- compliance with the statutory obligations under Section 134(c) and Section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The insurer has also denied the age, avocation, income of the deceased, as well as the relationship and dependency of the petitioners upon the deceased, and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

10. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Chowdaiah S.R. died in the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 06-05-2023 at about 2.45 p.m. near D- Cross Circle, Doddaballapura Town, due to rash or negligence driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-17-MA-1497 by its driver ?

3
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and Dependents of deceased ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

if so, what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award ?
11.
In support of their claim, Petitioner No.2/Son of deceased is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.17.
Further, CMO of General hospital, Doddaballapura is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.18 to 23.
Respondent No.3 has examined its official as RW-1 and got marked her authorization letter as Ex.R.1.
Owner of offending car is examined as RW-2 and no documents are got marked.
12. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

13. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.4 : As per the final order, for the following:
REASON 14. ISSUE NO.1

Petitioners say that on 06.05.2023 at about 2:45 P.M., the deceased, Chowdaiah,
was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-06-EZ-1327.

The rider was riding the said motorcycle on the Bengaluru-Gowribidanur Road, near D-cross Circle,
Doddaballapura Town, Bengaluru District.
At that time, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the motorcycle.
15. Due to the tremendous impact of the accident, both the rider and the pillion rider sustained severe injuries all over their bodies.

Immediately after the accident, Chowdaiah was shifted to Aster CMI Hospital, Bengaluru, where despite expert medical treatment, he succumbed to the fatal injuries on 08.05.2023 at about 11:20 P.M.
16.

In order to substantiate their case, the petitioners have produced documentary evidence marked at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10, namely FIR, Complaint, Requisition for statement, Spot Mahazar, Inquest Report, IMV Report, Rough Sketch, Charge Sheet and Post-Mortem Report.

17. On the other hand, Respondent No.1 has specifically contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle on which the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider.
It is alleged that the rider violated traffic rules by jumping the red signal and that the deceased was not wearing a helmet.
It is further contended that the accident did not occur due to any negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car.

Sridevi vs Srinivas R on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186578833/
4 18.

Respondent No.3 (Insurance Company) has also contended that there was no involvement of the offending car in the alleged accident and that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the motorcycle rider.
In order to substantiate the said defence, an official of Respondent No.3 was examined as RW1 and the owner of the offending car was examined as RW2.
Both witnesses reiterated the contents of their respective written statements.
19. However, there exists no serious dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident and the fact that the deceased sustained fatal injuries in the said accident.

The documentary evidence produced by the petitioners, particularly the FIR, Spot Mahazar, Rough Sketch and Charge Sheet, clearly establish that the accident occurred on the road in the manner alleged and that the collision was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
20. The Investigating Officer, after due investigation, has filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending car.
The said charge sheet has not been challenged before any competent court.
The inquest report and post-mortem report further establish that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the said road traffic accident.
21. Though RW1 and RW2 have denied negligence, nothing substantial has been elicited in the cross-examination to probabilise their defence.

No independent witness, counter-complaint,
alternative sketch or rebuttal investigation report has been produced to support their contention.

Mere denial and bald allegations that the motorcycle rider was negligent or that the deceased was not wearing a helmet cannot displace the consistent and corroborated documentary evidence produced by the petitioners.
22. There is no material placed on record to contradict the testimony of PW1, which is consistent and duly supported by the contemporaneous police records.
23. It is well settled that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation and the proceedings before the Tribunal are summary in nature.
The Tribunal is not required to insist upon strict proof of negligence as required in a criminal trial.
When the police investigation culminates in filing of a charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the same remains unchallenged, it carries strong prima facie evidentiary value.

24. On careful appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car, which resulted in fatal injuries to the deceased Chowdaiah, who subsequently succumbed to the said injuries.
Hence I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
25. ISSUE NO.2 and 3: To avoid repetition, Issue Nos. 2 and 3 are taken together for common discussion.
26. The petitioners contend that they are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased.

In order to establish their relationship with the deceased, the petitioners have produced Aadhaar Cards marked at Ex.P12 and Ex.P13, which clearly Sridevi vs Srinivas R on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186578833/
5 indicate their relationship with the deceased.

sentences.text: The respondents have also not seriously disputed the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.
Hence, the petitioners are treated as the legal representatives of the deceased.

27. The petitioners have contended that the deceased Dr. Chowdaiah was a qualified medical practitioner who had served in the Government service as a Gynecologist and had retired from the said service.

It is further stated that even after his retirement, considering his vast experience,
professional skill, and caliber in the medical field, the services of the deceased were required by the Government Hospital and therefore he was engaged to work as a doctor on contract basis at the General Hospital, Doddaballapur.
28. In order to substantiate the avocation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P14 - Contract Agreement and Ex.P15 - Bank Statement.

Further, the Chief Medical Officer of General Hospital, Doddaballapur was examined as PW2, who has produced documents marked at Ex.P19 to Ex.P23, namely the contract agreement, salary certificate, Form-16A,
attendance register and gazetted notification dated 07.06.2023.
29.

On careful appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, it is evident that the deceased was engaged by the said hospital as a contract doctor and he was being paid a salary for the services rendered by him.

The salary certificate marked at Ex.P20 clearly discloses that the deceased was drawing a gross monthly salary of Rs.1,10,000/-
for the period from April 2022 to April 2023 and Rs.58,667/- for the period of May 2023.
30.
During the course of cross-examination, PW2 has stated that the formal contract of the deceased was valid up to 31.03.2023 and thereafter it had not been immediately renewed.
However, PW2 has specifically deposed that the deceased had obtained oral permission from the District Health Officer (DHO) and continued to render his services in the hospital even thereafter.
It is also evident from Ex.P23 - Gazette Notification dated 07.06.2023 that permission was subsequently granted to continue such contract engagement.

31. The evidence on record therefore clearly indicates that even after retirement from Government service, the deceased continued to serve the society by rendering his professional services as a doctor on contract basis.

Considering the professional qualification, experience, and caliber of the deceased as a medical practitioner, it is quite natural that his services were retained by the hospital even after retirement.
The materials available on record establish that the deceased was actively practicing and was earning a regular income from the said contract engagement.

32. The documentary evidence such as salary certificate, contract agreement, attendance records and Form-16A further corroborate the case of the petitioners that the deceased was earning Rs.1,10,000/- per month from his contractual employment.
Therefore, this Tribunal finds no reason to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners with regard to the avocation and income of the deceased.

Sridevi vs Srinivas R on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186578833/
6 33.

Hence, taking into consideration the oral evidence of PW1 and PW2 coupled with the documentary evidence available on record, this Tribunal holds that the deceased was working as a contract doctor at General Hospital, Doddaballapur and was earning Rs.1,10,000/- per month at the time of the accident.
If the deceased had been alive, he would have continued the said profession and earned the said income for the benefit of his family.
Accordingly, the monthly income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.1,10,000/- for the purpose of calculating compensation.

34. The learned counsel for the respondent no 3 contended that Petitioner No.1 (wife) is receiving pension and Petitioner No.2 (son) is a Civil Engineer earning about Rs.8,00,000 per annum, and therefore they cannot be treated as dependents of the deceased.

In support of the said contention,
reliance was placed on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.47/2015 c/w MFA No.68/2017 between United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Mallika George and others,
wherein the Court held that when the claimants are not dependent on the income of the deceased,
compensation under the head of loss of dependency cannot be granted.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Mallika George and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held that while determining loss of dependency, the actual financial loss suffered by the dependents has to be considered.

35. The respondent has also relied upon the decision reported in 2019 (2) AKR 580 - Sulochana Sanganabasava Matti and others vs. Mohammed Saleem and others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court held that when the claimants are not dependent on the income of the deceased, they are not entitled to compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
36.

Further reliance was placed on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal Nos.
24110-24112/2023 - Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Bhagatsingh Rawat and others, wherein it was held that the amount under the head of loss of consortium should not be granted separately to each dependent, but should be awarded in terms of the principles laid down in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680.
37.

sentences.text: Another decision relied upon is MFA No.6818/2019 - Puttamma and others vs. Managing Director, BMTC, wherein the Hon'ble High Court observed that when the claimants are not dependents, appropriate deductions towards personal expenses must be made.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 38. Further reliance was placed on MFA No.22123/2012 c/w MFA 24125/2012 - Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Shakuntalamma and others, wherein it was held that consortium cannot be awarded to persons who are not legally entitled.

39. Further reliance was placed on MFA No.5465/2016 National Insurance Co Ltd V T.Chandranaika and other wherein it is held that when there is only one dependent of the deceased,
the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be taken as .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 40. Keeping in view of above said dictum, once again I have perused the material available on record.
It is admitted by PW1 during cross-examination that Petitioner No.2 is a Civil Engineer and is earning about Rs.8,00,000 per annum.
Therefore, Petitioner No.2 cannot be considered as a dependent on the income of the deceased.

However, Petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased is Sridevi vs Srinivas R on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186578833/
7 considered as a dependent.

As per the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation and above said decisions, when there is only one dependent,
50% of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, 50% of the income of the deceased is deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Then the annual income would come to (Rs.55,000/- X 12) Rs.6,60,000/- and applying 5 multiplier, Petitioners are awarded Rs.33,00,000/- towards loss of dependency.
41. CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others., this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled .44,000/- each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 has lost his father.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 42. Loss to estate:
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband and the petitioner No.2 has lost his father.
Hence, .20,000/- is awarded towards loss to estate.
43. Funeral Expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent .2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award .16,500/- for the funeral and other incidental expenses.

44. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :
Sl.No Nature of Compensation Amount 1. Loss of dependency Rs. 33,00,000/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs. 88,000/-
to Petitioner No.1 and 2 3. Loss to estate Rs. 20,000/-
4. Transportation of Rs. 16,500/-
dead body, Funeral & obsequies Expenses Total Rs. 34,24,500/-
45.
Liability:
The Petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 3 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I answer issue no.2 in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of .34,24,500/-/- together with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.3 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is apportioned to the Petitioner No.2 and remaining entire amount is apportioned to the petitioner No.1.

Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.1, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to her through E-payment on proper identification.
The entire amount apportioned to petitioner No.2 with interest shall be disbursed to him through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Mere denial and bald allegations that the motorcycle rider was negligent or that the deceased was not wearing a helmet cannot displace the consistent and corroborated documentary evidence produced by the petitioners.
22. There is no material placed on record to contradict the testimony of PW1, which is consistent and duly supported by the contemporaneous police records.
23. It is well settled that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation and the proceedings before the Tribunal are summary in nature.
The Tribunal is not required to insist upon strict proof of negligence as required in a criminal trial.
When the police investigation culminates in filing of a charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the same remains unchallenged, it carries strong prima facie evidentiary value.
Considering the professional qualification, experience, and caliber of the deceased as a medical practitioner, it is quite natural that his services were retained by the hospital even after retirement.
The materials available on record establish that the deceased was actively practicing and was earning a regular income from the said contract engagement.
Therefore, Petitioner No.2 cannot be considered as a dependent on the income of the deceased.
However, Petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased is Sridevi vs Srinivas R on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186578833/
7 considered as a dependent.
As per the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation and above said decisions, when there is only one dependent,
50% of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.

Hence, .20,000/- is awarded towards loss to estate.
43. Funeral Expenses:
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award .16,500/- for the funeral and other incidental expenses.

Hence the Respondent No.1 and 3 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I answer issue no.2 in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioners are awarded compensation of .34,24,500/-/- together with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.3 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is apportioned to the Petitioner No.2 and remaining entire amount is apportioned to the petitioner No.1.
Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.1, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to her through E-payment on proper identification.
The entire amount apportioned to petitioner No.2 with interest shall be disbursed to him through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
